text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: This research article presents a spatially explicit Agent Based Model (ABM) integrated with GIS to simulate future urban growth and land use changes across Kuwait, a national-scale study area. The primary focus is on land use/land cover (LULC) prediction through modeling future urban development patterns under two scenarios (business-as-usual and adaptive growth), with mapped outputs of projected land use to 2050. The study implements multiple future scenarios with quantitative comparison of impacts such as housing shortage and traffic congestion. The model is calibrated and validated against historical spatial data (1995–2015), and quantitative metrics such as similarity of predicted vs. real urban form (80%) and correlation coefficients are reported. The modeling is spatially explicit at the district level, covering the entire country of Kuwait. The study includes scenario-based quantitative spatial projections, meeting all core inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria. Although the focus is on urban growth (a subset of LULC), the work clearly falls within national-scale LULC future prediction research.)
